memos.headline: AAPL and GOOGL Lead at 52-Week Highs; NVDA and PG Show Deteriorating Relative Strength
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the mega-cap universe today. AAPL sits at its 52-week high with RSI 68 and +11% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — strong trend, not yet overbought, and I want to stay long until a close below the 50-day moving average (roughly $263). GOOGL is the strongest name on the board with +90% over 26 weeks and +32.6% relative strength over 12 weeks, but RSI at 73.5 and a +19.5% premium to the 50-day mean screams near-term exhaustion risk; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. On the weak side, NVDA is 14.5% off its high with RSI 41.5 and -13.3% relative strength over 4 weeks — this is a broken short-term trend and I'd avoid until it reclaims the 50-day. PG is in a persistent downtrend, trading 6.9% below its 200-day mean with -12.2% relative strength over 12 weeks, and I see no reason to own it here.

views.note: At 52-week high, RSI 68, strong relative strength; would reassess on a close below ~$263 (50-day area).
Dominant relative strength (+32.6% vs SPY 12w) but RSI 73.5 and +19.5% above 50d mean raise near-term pullback risk; size accordingly.
Up 37% over 12 weeks with +31.7% relative strength, RSI 62.9 not yet overbought, only 1.7% off high; invalidated below ~$528 (50-day area).
Healthy uptrend above both moving averages but flat 4-week relative strength vs SPY; no edge either way near term.
Bounced +7.4% this week but still -8.2% from high and -6.3% relative strength over 12 weeks; needs to clear $254 area to confirm trend resumption.
RSI 41.5, -14.5% drawdown, -13.3% relative strength over 4 weeks — broken short-term trend; would reconsider above $187 (50-day area).
Below 50-day mean, -6.9% relative strength over 4 weeks, RSI 45 — lagging badly; needs to reclaim $510 to turn constructive.
Persistent downtrend: -6.9% below 200-day, -17.6% drawdown, -12.2% relative strength over 12 weeks — no sign of a bottom.
Catastrophic -46% drawdown from 52-week high and trading 10% below 200-day mean; structurally damaged, avoid until sustained reclaim of 200-day.
Flat relative strength, RSI 49.9, close to both moving averages — no directional signal; range-bound.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA, which posted $57.01B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a 56.0% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt — an extraordinary combination of growth and profitability. GOOGL delivered $102.35B in revenue (+15.9% YoY) at a 34.2% net margin on a clean $14.79B debt load, making it the best risk-adjusted earner among the mega-caps. MSFT's 18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin remain impressive, though net income growth of 12.5% lagged revenue growth, suggesting some operating cost pressure I want to monitor. On the other side, UNH's net margin collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth, and $80.14B in total debt makes this a name I cannot own until I see margin stabilization. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% with net income down 12.3%, reflecting commodity headwinds that compress cash flow in a way I'm unwilling to underwrite at current levels.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, and minimal leverage of $8.47B make this the strongest earnings compounder in the universe; a margin decline below 45% would change my view.
15.9% revenue growth with a 34.2% net margin and low $14.79B debt offers durable, high-quality earnings; I'd reassess if ad revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
18.4% top-line growth and 35.7% net margin are strong, but net income growth lagging at 12.5% signals cost absorption I need to watch in coming quarters.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4% YoY) with net margin expanding to 11.8% and net income up 38.2% shows operating leverage kicking in; margin sustainability is the key variable.
Revenue grew 7.9% and net income surged 86.4% (likely off a depressed base), but $90.68B in total debt and modest top-line growth limit my conviction on forward earnings power.
Solid 31.0% net margin and 11.6% net income growth, but the bank's $427.20B debt load and rate-cycle sensitivity keep me on the sideline.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but only 3.0% revenue growth limits upside in a portfolio context.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, implying margin compression to 13.0%; I need to see cost discipline before getting constructive.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% net margin on $80.14B of debt — this is textbook cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for until margins recover.
Revenue down 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin reflect commodity-driven earnings erosion; I'd reconsider only if oil prices firm and margins rebound above 12%.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Meets Sticky Inflation and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Fade Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 75bp over 12 months to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone, while the 10y yield has drifted lower to 4.02%. However, the macro backdrop is not clean — CPI is running at 3.0% YoY and unemployment has risen 30bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.4%, painting a mild stagflationary picture. The curve has re-steepened dramatically (+46bp YoY on the 10y-2y spread to +0.55pp), consistent with the market pricing further front-end easing but some term premium for inflation risk. I have moderate conviction that this regime favors duration-sensitive growth names (big-cap tech) and defensive staples, while cyclicals and energy face headwinds from softening labor markets. A CPI print breaking materially above 3.5% YoY or unemployment spiking past 4.7% would force me to reassess toward a harder-landing or re-tightening scenario.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling front-end rates and declining 10y yields; strong secular positioning in a slowing economy.
Lower rates support multiples for mega-cap tech, though consumer softness from rising unemployment tempers conviction slightly.
Easing cycle and falling long rates are tailwinds for high-duration growth, but 3% headline CPI keeps some risk of a policy pause.
Defensive staples should outperform as unemployment trends higher and the economy softens; lower rates reduce discount-rate drag on stable cash flows.
Steeper curve is a positive for NIM, but rising unemployment and easing cycle compress front-end lending margins — offsetting forces.
Rising unemployment and slowing labor market signal cyclical deceleration; industrial capex likely to soften.
Softening demand backdrop from rising unemployment is a headwind for energy; easing cycle historically coincides with weaker commodity demand.
Benefits from lower discount rates on long-duration cash flows and consumer resilience in e-commerce even as labor market softens.
Lower rates are supportive but ad revenue cyclicality and 3% CPI creating margin uncertainty keep me on the sideline.
Defensive healthcare is attractive in a slowdown, but regulatory and political uncertainty limits macro-driven conviction.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: AMZN and CAT Surged While MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Positioning Implications for Late November
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal available across the universe. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) saw outsized positive reactions on their Q3 prints, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have legs, though nearly a month has passed and some of that enthusiasm is likely priced. MSFT (-2.9%) and NVDA (-3.2%) both sold off on results, and NVDA's reaction is the freshest (Nov 19-20), meaning negative sentiment may still be weighing. UNH has had a flurry of governance-related 8-Ks — bylaws changes, officer departures — which in my experience signals organizational noise that media can amplify negatively, even though the earnings reaction was a benign +0.5%. I have highest conviction on AMZN's positive momentum and NVDA's near-term sentiment headwind, and lower conviction on the quieter names like PG and XOM where reactions were negligible and filing activity is routine.

views.note: Massive +9.6% earnings-day pop and a follow-up 8-K on Nov 20 suggest sustained positive narrative, though a month of digestion tempers conviction.
The +11.6% earnings reaction was the largest in the universe, signaling a strong sentiment inflection, but the move is nearly a month old and likely partially priced.
Fresh -3.2% sell-off on Nov 19-20 earnings print suggests negative sentiment is still being absorbed and crowded expectations may need further resetting.
The -2.9% earnings reaction on Oct 29-30 points to disappointed expectations; with no subsequent positive catalysts in the filing record, tone likely remains soft.
Benign +0.5% earnings reaction but a cluster of governance filings including officer departures and bylaws changes could feed negative media narratives.
Flat +0.2% earnings reaction and routine follow-on filings suggest no meaningful sentiment shift in either direction.
Negligible -0.4% earnings reaction implies the market had already priced the result; no subsequent filings to shift the narrative.
Flat -0.3% earnings reaction and a string of routine 8-Ks (officer changes, other events) generate no discernible sentiment signal.
Solid +2.5% earnings pop and a follow-up 8-K suggest modestly positive tone, though the move is smaller than AMZN/CAT and conviction is moderate.
The -1.9% earnings reaction was mildly negative but subsequent filings are routine; sentiment appears to have stabilized without a clear directional shift.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Falling Oil Signal Geopolitical Crosscurrents for US Equities
memos.body: I see a mixed but structurally cautious geopolitical backdrop as of today. The economic policy uncertainty index sits at 334.67, down 13% over the past month but still up 24% over three months, suggesting that while acute trade-policy fears may have eased near-term, the structural overhang from tariff and export-control regimes remains elevated. VIX at 17.21 has risen 16% over three months, consistent with markets pricing in policy tail risk. WTI crude at $58.81 is down nearly 8% over three months, which I read as reflecting both demand-side concerns (possibly China slowdown) and a loosening of energy supply constraints—a headwind for XOM but a modest tailwind for cost-sensitive industrials and consumer staples. HY spreads widening 22 bps over three months to 3.00% confirm that credit markets are beginning to price incremental macro and policy risk. I would need to see a concrete rollback of semiconductor export controls or a formal US-China trade framework to upgrade my stance on the most exposed names.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls to China remain the dominant structural risk; elevated policy uncertainty index (+24% 3m) and no evidence of de-escalation keep me cautious.
Supply-chain concentration in China is a known risk but partially mitigated by diversification; policy uncertainty is high but not worsening month-over-month.
WTI at $58.81 and falling 7.5% over three months pressures upstream margins; multiple 8-K filings suggest active corporate adjustments but the commodity backdrop is unfavorable.
Lower oil prices reduce input costs for infrastructure projects, but elevated policy uncertainty and potential tariff exposure on imported components keep me on the sideline.
Defensive consumer staples benefit from falling energy costs and are less exposed to export-control or tariff escalation; four recent 8-Ks suggest active investor communication.
Widening HY spreads (+22 bps 3m) and a flattening yield curve (10y-2y at 0.55, down 10 bps 3m) create offsetting forces for bank earnings; geopolitical risk is a wash here.

plan.summary: Overweight high-conviction names where technical, fundamental, and macro analysts converge (AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN), with a moderate allocation to CAT on strong technicals and sentiment despite macro caution. Hold ~25% cash to buffer elevated policy uncertainty and mild stagflationary crosscurrents.

plans.rationale: Strongest technical setup (52-week high, RSI 68, +11% relative strength) with macro tailwind from falling rates. Fundamentals analyst is only neutral on modest revenue growth, but three of five analysts are constructive, making this the highest-consensus long.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 50-day moving average (~$263) or a sudden spike in CPI above 3.5% that threatens the rate-easing narrative.

plans.rationale: Best fundamental profile among mega-caps (34.2% net margin, 15.9% revenue growth, low debt) and dominant relative strength (+32.6% vs SPY). Sized slightly below AAPL because technicals flag near-term exhaustion risk (RSI 73.5, +19.5% above 50d) and macro analyst is only neutral on ad cyclicality.
plans.changes_my_mind: RSI breaks above 80 without a pullback (blow-off risk) or ad revenue growth decelerates below 10% in next quarterly update.

plans.rationale: Strong fundamental momentum (13.4% revenue growth, net income +38.2%, margin expanding to 11.8%) and the largest positive earnings sentiment signal (+9.6% pop). Technical analyst is neutral pending a break above $254, so I size moderately and use a wider stop.
plans.changes_my_mind: Failure to reclaim and hold $254 area within two weeks, or net margin contracting below 10% in next quarter.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst highlights strong momentum (+37% over 12w, RSI 62.9, near highs) and sentiment analyst notes the largest earnings-day pop in the universe (+11.6%). However, fundamentals show margin compression (net income -6.7%) and macro/geopolitics analysts flag cyclical headwinds from rising unemployment and tariff risk, so I size down meaningfully.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 50-day (~$528) or unemployment rising above 4.7% in the next jobs report.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals remain strong (18.4% revenue growth, 35.7% net margin) and macro analyst favors duration-sensitive growth in an easing cycle. However, technicals are weak (below 50d, RSI 45) and sentiment is soft post-earnings (-2.9%), so this is a small position betting on mean reversion.
plans.changes_my_mind: Continued deterioration below $475 or net income growth decelerating further in next quarter.

plans.rationale: Healthy uptrend above moving averages and solid 31% net margin, but all five analysts are essentially neutral with offsetting forces (steeper curve vs rising unemployment, flat relative strength). Tiny position as a diversifier.
plans.changes_my_mind: HY spreads widening above 3.5% or a close below the 50-day moving average.
